channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: US President Donald Trump signs order to ease limits on diesel variety to curb costs
item.description: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order to ease restrictions on the use of a tax-exempt variety of diesel, Bloomberg reported on Monday.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis claim missile, drone strikes on multiple targets in Saudi Arabia
item.description: Yemen's Houthi group said on Monday that it carried out three military operations using ballistic and cruise missiles and drones against airports, an oil facility, and military sites across Saudi Arabia, Xinhua News Agency reported.

item.title: The Japanese Yen firms on a BoJ speech about AI and gives it all back
item.description: Bank of Japan (BoJ) Governor Ueda speaks on Tuesday at 06:35 GMT, and his first major remarks since the September 18 hike to 1.25% are the next test of October hike bets. Traders give a second hike on October 30 about a one-in-four chance.

item.title: Gold holds steady below $4,150 amid elevated US yields
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) trades on a flat note near $4,140 during the early Asian session on Tuesday. Pressure from a stronger US Dollar (USD) and elevated US Treasury yields was offset by reduced expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike this month.

item.title: Australian Dollar defies rising yields as AUD/USD closes in on 0.70
item.description: The Aussie Dollar registers back-to-back days of gains on Monday, even though US Treasury yields edged higher, underpinning the US Dollar, which appreciated against a basket of six currencies but not versus the Australian Dollar. The AUD/USD trades at 0.6972, up 0.37%.

item.title: The New Zealand Dollar holds near its lows while business confidence jumps
item.description: New Zealand's firms are more upbeat and raising fewer prices, and the second half of that matters more for the Kiwi. NZD/USD trades just above 0.5600 after a fresh low beneath it, back near its November 2025 low.

item.title: US Treasury yields scale multi-year highs as inflation fears return
item.description: US Treasury yields edged up at the beginning of the week, with the 30- and 10-year yields reaching multi-year highs as inflation expectations rose, as shown in a US Institute for Supply Management (ISM) survey indicating that business activity in the services sector slowed while input prices surged.

item.title: The Euro breaks to a fresh low, then bounces, as Spain calls a snap vote
item.description: Reports that Spain's government was preparing an early election pushed EUR/USD to its lowest since May 2025, and hedge-fund selling in Asia set off option barriers that deepened the fall, traders said. The pair has since recovered more than half of that drop and trades back above 1.1200.

item.title: The Pound flatlines as Treasury yields climb to another high
item.description: The odds of an October Fed hike have fallen from about two in three in late September to roughly one in five, and GBP/USD hasn't left the range it has traded in since September 24. Monday's range is entirely inside Friday's, and the pair trades just above 1.3200.

item.title: Mexican Peso builds winning streak as USD/MXN drifts toward 18.00
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) posted back-to-back bullish days as USD/MXN edges lower by about 0.34% on Monday amid softer-than-expected US data and a mediocre Nonfarm Payrolls report last Friday. The exotic pair trades at 18.08 after peaking near 18.26.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS seen very slightly tightening – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Edward Lee expects the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to deliver another very slight tightening in October, raising the SGD NEER slope to 1.5% from 1.25% while keeping the band parameters unchanged.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD builds base above $60, eyes $64
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price drifts higher by over 1.14% on Monday, even as US Treasury yields rise and the Greenback extends its gains by 0.26%, as per the US Dollar Index (DXY). XAG/USD trades at $61.13, after bouncing off daily lows of $60.36.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Sideways with firmer bias against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategist Quek Ser Leang reports USD/CNH slipped to 6.7008 before closing at 6.7041, with intraday price action expected to stay between 6.7000 and 6.7105. For the coming 1–3 weeks, he continues to see the pair confined to a 6.6950–6.7270 range.

item.title: Gold stalls below $4,150 as rising US yields offset Fed relief
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) prices drift lower on Monday as a strong US Dollar and high US Treasury yields undermine the precious metal, which has failed to rally as investors expect a less hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) and have priced out a rate hike this month.

item.title: Markets just priced out rate hikes on financial stress. This chart shows why 2022-23 says they’ll be wrong
item.description: Traders have taken about one quarter-point hike out of their European Central Bank (ECB) forecasts since mid-September, betting the ECB will stop raising rates because of a French debt selloff.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens as wide yield gap supports US Dollar
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) remains on the back foot against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday as the wide yield differential continues to favour the Greenback, while broader structural headwinds weigh on the Japanese currency. At the time of writing, USD/JPY trades around 158.10, up 0.17% on the day.

item.title: Forex Today: PMIs in Europe and Fedspeak will do the rounds
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) has picked up extra pace on Monday, reaching fresh tops on the back of persistent safe-haven demand, while fiscal concerns in Europe continued to weigh on the broader risk complex.

item.title: United States: Domestic rare earth production push – ING
item.description: ING’s report by Coco Zhang and Ewa Manthey explains how the United States is enhancing domestic Rare earth production. Federal support now includes grants, loans, equity stakes, purchase agreements and price floors for key products like NdPr oxide and magnets.

item.title: British Pound slides as France fiscal shock lifts the US Dollar
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) dives more than 0.19% against the US Dollar (USD) at the beginning of the week, despite a dip in US services sector activity and elevated US Treasury yields. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3218 at the time of writing.

item.title: EUR/CHF Price Forecast: 100-day SMA limits immediate downside
item.description: EUR/CHF holds modest losses on Monday as growing fiscal concerns in France weigh on the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Australian Dollar edges higher despite robust US services
item.description: AUD/USD advances on Monday, trading around 0.6970 at the time of writing, up 0.34% on the day. The pair manages to gain ground despite persistent strength in the US Dollar (USD), which remains supported by elevated Treasury yields and weakness in the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Euro: Fiscal stress and fewer ECB hikes weigh against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports the Euro (EUR) is underperforming major currencies, with EUR/USD briefly hitting 1.1161, its lowest since May 2025. Elias Haddad flags France’s budget crisis spilling into wider Eurozone bond markets and complicating potential European Central Bank (ECB) Transmission Protection Instrument activation, leaving the Euro pressured by rising fiscal risk and expectations of a shallower ECB hiking cycle.

item.title: Dollar Index hits an 18-month high on French debt fears
item.description: France's government owes close to 120% of what its economy produces in a year. The gap between what France and Germany pay to borrow for 10 years reached about 1.5 percentage points on Friday, the widest since 2011.

item.title: Gold trades flat as stronger US Dollar offsets easing Fed rate-hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) (XAU/USD) lacks clear directional momentum on Monday. A stronger US Dollar and elevated US Treasury yields cap the upside, while easing Federal Reserve (Fed) interest-rate hike bets cushion the downside. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,142, little changed on the day.

item.title: Canadian Dollar attracts fresh buying after touching multi-month low
item.description: USD/CAD reverses its earlier gains on Monday as the Canadian Dollar (CAD) outperforms its major peers, while the US Dollar (USD) consolidates after mixed US business activity data.

item.title: South Korean Won: Strong exports and policy support KRW – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Moses Lim notes that USD/KRW declined on Friday and over the week as robust South Korean exports and supportive policy actions bolstered the Korean Won. Elevated but easing inflation allows the Bank of Korea to stay hawkish while likely holding rates in October.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Limited relief, challenging backdrop – OCBC
item.description: Christopher Wong at OCBC expects the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) to see some near-term relief from softer United States (US) payrolls and a wider trade surplus, with policymakers emphasizing IDR stability.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range trade holds against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategist Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD slipped to 1.2781 on Friday, with the SGD NEER staying well above its midpoint. For the intraday session, he expects the pair to hold within 1.2768–1.2832, aligning with technical levels at 1.2775/1.2815. On a 1–3 week and 1–3 month horizon, he still sees scope for a recovery toward 1.2835 while 1.2765 acts as strong support.

item.title: Euro falls back below 1.1200 as US Dollar dominates despite weaker ISM Services PMI
item.description: EUR/USD falls 0.60% on Monday and trades around 1.1190 at the time of writing. The pair remains under pressure as the US Dollar (USD) maintains positive momentum, supported in part by elevated US Treasury yields, while political and fiscal concerns in Europe weigh on the Euro (EUR).

item.title: US Dollar: Upside risks persist as data watched – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad notes the Dollar rallied broadly last week as DXY hit new cyclical highs alongside widening US-G6 rate differentials and a deepening global bond selloff.
